newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Bradesco launches Level One ADR.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Bradesco launches Level One ADR.

text.p: Brazil's largest private bank Bradesco said it launched its Level One ADR program Thursday following approval by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
The bank's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) began trading today on the U.S. over-the-counter market, said Carlos Alberto de Moraes, an official at Bradesco asset management department.
Moraes said Bradesco's decision to launch Level One ADRs is aimed at increasing the bank's profile among U.S. investors.
He said Bradesco plans to upgrade its ADR program to Level Two or Three in the future, but no timeframe has been set yet.
The ADRs are backed by existing preferred shares, the bank said in a published statement. Each ADR represents 1,000 non-voting shares.
It also said Citicorp's Citibank N.A. is the issuer bank, while Bradesco is the custodian bank.
